notes: Decision maker: CTO Elisa Marquez (wants deterministic latency during trading hours).
Primary ask: dedicated capacity with throughput guarantees for peak market windows and deterministic fallbacks.

SLA specifics requested by customer: 99.99% monthly uptime objective; P1 support 1-hour response, P2 4-hour, P3 24-hour; scheduled maintenance limited to 02:00-05:00 local on Sundays and excluded from quarter ends.

Credit schedule proposed by Summit: if uptime < 99.99% then 10% credit; < 99.95% then 25% credit; < 99.0% then 100% credit up to one month invoice (cap requested). Legal wants firm caps and recovery SLAs for KV cache/stateful failures.

Throughput/latency targets from customer: sustained 150 RPS during peak windows, burst to 500 RPS for 15-minute intervals; p95 gen latency <= 120ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens), p95 <= 300ms for longer context workloads. Redwood's baseline POC results currently at p95 210ms with 4x A100.

Reserved GPU planning: Summit prefers 8x A100 80GB reserved with autoscaling headroom (burst pool + warm standby). Wants explicit cold-start bounds for new model rollouts and KV cache warmup guidance.
Routing/fallback: request automatic fallback to a quantized cheaper variant in different region (must honor data residency), or to nearline tier for non-critical reranking paths.
Security/compliance: must support company-managed KMS (HSM), SSO via SAML, 1 year audit log retention and monthly access reports. Data residency for EU customers (subset of traffic) required.
Quote from CTO on call: "We cannot afford regressions during settlement windows — need hard SLOs and transparent credit mechanics."
